section: Defence indigenisation - Make in India in defence, DAP 2020, iDEX, defence corridors, FDI in defence

accepted.s: With reference to the procurement categories under DAP 2020, which one has the HIGHEST priority?
accepted.x: Buy (Indian-IDDM) is the highest-priority procurement category under DAP 2020.
accepted.tq: Use the priority-order clue and distinguish the two closely related Indian procurement categories.
accepted.sec: DAP 2020 - procurement categories and priority order

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Buy (Indian-IDDM):
1. IDDM stands for Indigenously Designed, Developed and Manufactured.
2. The category was first added in DPP 2016.
3. It was introduced on the advice of the Dhirendra Singh Committee.
4. It is the least preferred category under DAP 2020.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because Buy (Indian-IDDM) is the most preferred category under DAP 2020.
accepted.tq: Find the single reversed-priority statement among the otherwise precise factual statements.
accepted.sec: DAP 2020 - procurement categories and priority order

accepted.s: DPP 2016, which introduced the Buy (Indian-IDDM) category, replaced which earlier procurement policy?
accepted.x: DPP 2016 replaced DPP 2013 and introduced the Buy (Indian-IDDM) category.
accepted.tq: Test the distinction between successive procurement policy documents and manuals.
accepted.sec: DAP 2020 - procurement categories and priority order

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the review initiated by the Ministry of Defence in 2025?
o: It declared 2025 the Year of Reforms and began reviewing DAP 2020 to support joint ventures and technology transfer for the private sector.
It reviewed DPP 2013 to expand only government-to-government procurement.
It declared 2025 the Year of Indigenisation and discontinued DAP 2020 completely.
It introduced DPM 2025 exclusively for capital procurement by the armed forces.
accepted.x: The Ministry of Defence declared 2025 the Year of Reforms and began reviewing DAP 2020 to support JVs and technology transfer for the private sector.
accepted.tq: Match the reform year with its stated objective and avoid confusing DAP with DPM.
accepted.sec: DAP 2020 - procurement categories and priority order

accepted.s: The Defence Procurement Manual (DPM) 2025 was released and made effective on which dates, respectively?
accepted.x: DPM 2025 was released on 23 October 2025 and took effect on 1 November 2025.
accepted.tq: Separate the release date from the date on which the measure came into force.
accepted.sec: DAP 2020 - procurement categories and priority order

accepted.s: The DPM 2025 covers approximately what amount of revenue procurement?
accepted.x: DPM 2025 covers approximately ₹1 lakh crore of revenue procurement.
accepted.tq: Identify the approximate scale rather than confusing revenue procurement with capital procurement.
accepted.sec: DAP 2020 - procurement categories and priority order

accepted.s: An Expression of Interest for 600 indigenous 1,000-kg aerial bombs was associated with which procurement category?
accepted.x: The EoI for 600 indigenous 1,000-kg aerial bombs was issued under Buy (Indian-IDDM).
accepted.tq: Apply the procurement-category definition to an indigenous manufacturing example.
accepted.sec: DAP 2020 - procurement categories and priority order

accepted.s: Under DAP 2020, offset clauses were dropped in which types of deals?
o: All Indian private-sector deals and all export contracts
accepted.x: DAP 2020 dropped offset clauses in government-to-government and single-vendor deals.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the two specified deal types from broader procurement categories.
accepted.sec: DAP 2020 - procurement categories and priority order

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Positive Indigenisation Lists:
1. Five Positive Indigenisation Lists have been issued.
2. They bar imports of listed items after specified dates.
3. The SRIJAN portal is associated with their implementation and indigenisation efforts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Five lists have been issued, imports of listed items are barred after set dates, and SRIJAN supports indigenisation.
accepted.tq: Check whether all components of a policy description belong to the same indigenisation framework.
accepted.sec: Positive indigenisation lists and iDEX - SRIJAN, ADITI, DISC

accepted.s: What is the principal function of the SRIJAN portal?
o: To provide export licences for defence equipment
To conduct recruitment for the armed forces
To enable DPSUs and the Services to list imported items that Indian industry can manufacture
accepted.x: SRIJAN is the indigenisation portal through which DPSUs and the Services list import items that Indian industry can manufacture.
accepted.tq: Use the portal-function distinction and avoid confusing SRIJAN with a funding scheme.
accepted.sec: Positive indigenisation lists and iDEX - SRIJAN, ADITI, DISC

accepted.s: iDEX was launched by the Prime Minister in:
accepted.x: Innovations for Defence Excellence, or iDEX, was launched by the Prime Minister in April 2018.
accepted.tq: Test the launch year of the innovation initiative against nearby defence-policy years.
accepted.sec: Positive indigenisation lists and iDEX - SRIJAN, ADITI, DISC

accepted.s: Which of the following groups is specifically associated with the working model of iDEX?
o: State governments and public-sector banks exclusively
Only DPSUs and the three Services
accepted.x: iDEX works with MSMEs, start-ups, innovators and academia to promote defence innovation.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct institutional participants and reject the exclusive-only formulation.
accepted.sec: Positive indigenisation lists and iDEX - SRIJAN, ADITI, DISC

accepted.s: By March 2026, iDEX had engaged how many start-ups and innovators, with an outlay of ₹498.78 crore?
accepted.x: By March 2026, iDEX had engaged 676 start-ups and innovators, with an outlay of ₹498.78 crore.
accepted.tq: Pair the exact count with the associated financial outlay.
accepted.sec: Positive indigenisation lists and iDEX - SRIJAN, ADITI, DISC

accepted.s: ADITI, under the iDEX framework, is intended primarily to fund deep-tech start-ups working in which areas?
o: Artificial intelligence, quantum technologies, hypersonics and directed energy
Conventional banking, insurance and retail technology
Agriculture, biotechnology, textiles and food processing
Mining, ports, railways and urban transport
accepted.x: ADITI funds deep-tech start-ups in artificial intelligence, quantum technologies, hypersonics and directed energy, with emphasis on critical and strategic defence technologies.
accepted.tq: Use the subject-area cluster to identify the defence deep-tech scheme.
accepted.sec: Positive indigenisation lists and iDEX - SRIJAN, ADITI, DISC

accepted.s: Which statement correctly describes the Defence India Startup Challenge (DISC)?
o: It is a list of imported defence items prohibited after a fixed date.
It is a corridor connecting defence manufacturing nodes in two States.
It consists of challenge rounds in which the Services set problem statements for start-ups to solve.
It is a procurement manual governing revenue expenditure.
accepted.x: DISC comprises iDEX challenge rounds in which the Services set problem statements for start-ups to solve.
accepted.tq: Match the institutional mechanism with its operational role rather than its name alone.
accepted.sec: Positive indigenisation lists and iDEX - SRIJAN, ADITI, DISC

accepted.s:
Which of the following are additional supports for defence innovation mentioned in this context?
1. Defence Testing Infrastructure Scheme
2. Technology Development Fund
3. Positive Indigenisation Lists
4. Defence India Startup Challenge
Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: The additional supports are the Defence Testing Infrastructure Scheme and the Technology Development Fund. Positive Indigenisation Lists and DISC are separate elements of the indigenisation and iDEX framework.
accepted.tq: Separate additional support mechanisms from the principal lists and challenge rounds.
accepted.sec: Positive indigenisation lists and iDEX - SRIJAN, ADITI, DISC

accepted.s: The Defence Innovation Organisation, which runs iDEX, is best described as:
o: A constitutional body created by Parliament
A private foreign consortium established by start-ups
A department of the Ministry of Finance
A not-for-profit organisation set up by HAL and BEL
accepted.x: iDEX is run by the Defence Innovation Organisation, a not-for-profit organisation set up by HAL and BEL.
accepted.tq: Ask who established the body and distinguish it from a ministry or constitutional institution.
accepted.sec: Positive indigenisation lists and iDEX - SRIJAN, ADITI, DISC

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the defence industrial corridor in which the node is located?
o: Lucknow — Uttar Pradesh Defence Industrial Corridor
Chennai — Uttar Pradesh Defence Industrial Corridor
Hosur — Uttar Pradesh Defence Industrial Corridor
Aligarh — Tamil Nadu Defence Industrial Corridor
accepted.x: Lucknow is a node of the Uttar Pradesh Defence Industrial Corridor. Chennai and Hosur are nodes of the Tamil Nadu corridor, while Aligarh is also in the Uttar Pradesh corridor.
accepted.tq: Start from a sure node and eliminate the options that cross the two corridors.
accepted.sec: Defence industrial corridors - states and nodes

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a node of the Uttar Pradesh Defence Industrial Corridor?
accepted.x: Salem is a node of the Tamil Nadu Defence Industrial Corridor. Lucknow, Kanpur, Jhansi and Chitrakoot are nodes of the Uttar Pradesh corridor.
accepted.tq: Find the one location belonging to the other corridor.
accepted.sec: Defence industrial corridors - states and nodes

accepted.s: Which of the following is the correct set of nodes of the Tamil Nadu Defence Industrial Corridor?
o: Hosur, Kanpur, Salem, Jhansi and Chitrakoot
Chennai, Hosur, Coimbatore, Salem and Tiruchirappalli
Chennai, Agra, Coimbatore, Aligarh and Salem
Lucknow, Kanpur, Agra, Aligarh and Jhansi
accepted.x: The Tamil Nadu corridor has nodes at Chennai, Hosur, Coimbatore, Salem and Tiruchirappalli.
accepted.tq: Recall the complete state-wise node list without mixing it with the Uttar Pradesh list.
accepted.sec: Defence industrial corridors - states and nodes

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about India’s defence industrial corridors:
1. There are two such corridors, one in Uttar Pradesh and one in Tamil Nadu.
2. They aim to provide infrastructure and incentives for decentralised defence manufacturing.
3. They are intended to support a connected defence manufacturing supply chain.
4. The BrahMos unit at Lucknow is associated with the Uttar Pradesh corridor.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The two corridors are in Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, and they support decentralised manufacturing and connected supply chains; the BrahMos unit at Lucknow is linked with the Uttar Pradesh corridor.
accepted.tq: Verify the number, purpose, supply-chain role and example together before selecting the combined option.
accepted.sec: Defence industrial corridors - states and nodes

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs concerning defence-related establishments in Andhra Pradesh is correctly matched?
o: BEL, Machilipatnam — opto-electronics and night vision
Naval Dockyard, Visakhapatnam — Western Naval Command headquarters
ADA flight-test complex, Sri Sathya Sai — ₹1,580.3 crore investment
BrahMos unit, Lucknow — Andhra Pradesh defence corridor node
accepted.x: BEL at Machilipatnam is associated with opto-electronics and night vision. The Naval Dockyard at Visakhapatnam is an Eastern Naval Command refit yard, and the ADA flight-test complex is valued at ₹15,803 crore.
accepted.tq: Match each establishment with its function or location and reject swapped authorities and figures.
accepted.sec: Defence industrial corridors - states and nodes

accepted.s: The Naval Dockyard at Visakhapatnam is described as the refit yard of which command?
accepted.x: The Naval Dockyard at Visakhapatnam is the Eastern Naval Command refit yard.
accepted.tq: Use the location-command relationship to distinguish the naval commands.
accepted.sec: Defence industrial corridors - states and nodes

accepted.s: The ADA flight-test complex at Sri Sathya Sai in Andhra Pradesh is associated with an investment of:
accepted.x: The ADA flight-test complex at Sri Sathya Sai is associated with an investment of ₹15,803 crore.
accepted.tq: Read the figure carefully and distinguish the position of the digit in the crore value.
accepted.sec: Defence industrial corridors - states and nodes

accepted.s: Which organisations were specifically identified as investing in Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: BDL and Kalyani Strategic Systems were identified as investing in Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Distinguish investing organisations from bodies that operate innovation portals or schemes.
accepted.sec: Defence industrial corridors - states and nodes
